site_or_subject: National data centre pause (from 2019) and capacity allocation calls DC-CFA (pilot, 2022-2023) and DC-CFA2 (2025-2026)
operator: IMDA / EDB (awardees: AirTrunk-ByteDance, Equinix, GDS, Microsoft; Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres, ST Telemedia Global Data Centres)
record: IMDA and EDB's release of 20 July 2022, launching the pilot Data Centre Call for Application (DC-CFA), states that the Government informed the industry of a temporary pause in the growth of DCs in 2019. On 14 July 2023 the agencies announced they were provisionally awarding about 80 MW to four proposals (AirTrunk-ByteDance consortium, Equinix, GDS, Microsoft), chosen from more than 20 proposals, with conditions including Green Mark DC Platinum certification; no per-awardee MW or site is given. DC-CFA2 was launched on 1 December 2025: At least 200MW of DC capacity would be made available; applicants must achieve a PUE of 1.25 (at 100% IT load) or better, be at least 50% powered by eligible green energy pathways, and obtain BCA-IMDA Green Mark for Data Centres 2024 Platinum; registration of interest closed on 5 December 2025. On 21 August 2026 the agencies provisionally allocated 200 megawatts (MW), 50MW each to Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, from more than 20 proposals; the DCs will locate on Jurong Island and will power more than 50% of their DC capacity from green energy sources. IMDA's Green Data Centre Roadmap states that Singapore has a total DC capacity exceeding 1.4 gigawatts and aims to provide at least 300 megawatts (MW) of additional capacity in the near term.

site_or_subject: Johor Data Centre Development Coordination Committee approvals, rejections and Tier 1/2 halt
operator: Johor State Government (DCDCC; Special Technical Committee)
record: Johor's committee (formally the Jawatankuasa Pembangunan Pusat Data Negeri Johor, JPPDNJ, which screens applications for zoning, infrastructure, water, electricity and buffer zones before they reach local authorities, under a state data-centre planning guideline approved in April 2024) began vetting applications in June 2024. In a 28 Nov 2024 state-assembly answer the Menteri Besar stated data centres must meet PUE not above 1.5 and WUE of 1.8; on 20 Nov 2025 exco Mohd Jafni Md Shukor told the assembly WUE must be below 1.8 under the planning guideline, with approval priority for applicants not using Syarikat Air Johor (SAJ) water. The state reported 42 approved projects to Q2 2025 and, in a Nov 2025 written answer, 17 operating data centres. The NST (19 Nov 2024) reports that the committee rejected nearly 30% of applications in five months and, per its vice-chairman Lee Ting Han, 4 of 14 foreign-operator bids, citing failure to show sustainable water/energy practices and sites lacking utility infrastructure; it gives Johor capacity as 10 MW in 2021 and ~1.3 GW in Nov 2024 [press, source not named for the 30% and capacity figures: New Straits Times]. The NST (27 Nov 2025) reports 51 approved projects (17 operational, 11 under construction and 23 at the approval stage) and that the state 'will no longer approve' Tier 1 and Tier 2 facilities, which it says can use up to 50 million litres/day versus ~200,000 L/day for Tier 3/4; data centres needing water must use reclaimed water rather than SAJ supply [press, source not named: New Straits Times].

site_or_subject: Viksit Gujarat Data Center Policy 2026-29 and Reliance-Meta Jamnagar site
operator: Government of Gujarat; Reliance Industries / Meta
record: Gujarat DST G.R. No. DST/MIT/e-file/24/2026/0624/IT (approved 06-08-2026) issues the Viksit Gujarat Data Center Policy (2026-29). Data-centre entities must source a minimum of 51% of electricity for core operations from green and renewable energy (§7.1). Incentives include 100% reimbursement of electricity duty actually paid for 20 years from commercial operation, power-tariff reimbursement of INR 1 per unit for 20 years, and capital support for captive desalination plants up to 20 MLD per GW of data-centre capacity (§6.1, §6.3); the State is to supply 24x7 water to the doorstep, and entities are 'expected' to meet water needs primarily from captive desalination where feasible (§6.5, §7.11). Only projects with approved IT load of 150 MW or above qualify, and total incentives are capped at 75% of Eligible Fixed Capital Investment (§7.2, §7.6). Data-centre operation is an 'Essential Service' under the Gujarat Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1972 (§8). The G.R. does not mention Jamnagar, Reliance, Meta or 168 MW.

gap: The area and capacity figures are JTC's and EDB's announcement, known here through a press report; no JTC land allocation or URA planning record for the park was found, and no document read gives its parcels, lot numbers or the plot of each DC-CFA2 awardee. Coordinates are for Jurong Island as a whole.
verification_note: EDB fact sheet fetched and its two Jurong Island sentences confirmed verbatim on a second read (2026-10-24). The 20ha and 700MW figures were read once in the JTC-hosted Straits Times article and not re-checked. (2026-10-24) The 20ha and 700MW figures are JTC's and EDB's announcement and moved to claim; the count of more than 70 data centres is the newspaper's own, marked as press with no source named; Jurong Island coordinates added.

site_or_subject: Energy Conservation Act registration scope and data centres
operator: National Environment Agency
record: NEA's registration page under the Energy Conservation Act sets an energy use threshold of 54 terajoules consumed per calendar year, attained in at least 2 of the 3 preceding years, at a single site, for corporations in three industry sectors: manufacturing and manufacturing-related services; supply of electricity, gas, steam, compressed air and chilled water for air-conditioning; and water supply and sewage and waste management. The page does not mention data centres and does not say whether a list of registered corporations or per-facility energy data is published.
